evidence: Receiving DO2 at decision time 52h = 9.22 mg/L (online sensor), minimum observed process-wide ~6.8 mg/L at 24-28h, both far above 2.0 mg/L limit
Receiving P(48h) = 2.909 g/L, consistent with source batches (2.98-3.06 g/L) at same age; no receiving-specific underperformance
Source batches under KEEP-like conditions peaked ~8.0-8.4 g/L at 72h then naturally declined, matching nominal model terminal 6.88 g/L
physical_forward_model(keep): below_limit_h=0, min DO 5.76 (pre-decision 8.53); sensitivity: 5/5 feasible, min DO 3.14-6.91, mass 576-583 kg
args.rationale: The receiving fermentation is operating normally and within oxygen constraints. Measured DO2 at the 52h decision point is 9.22 mg/L, with a process minimum of ~6.8 mg/L (during the 24-28h oxygen-demand peak), all comfortably above the 2.0 mg/L minimum. Product trajectory (P=2.91 g/L at 48h, delayed assay) tracks the source batches closely (2.98-3.06 g/L at same age), and source batches under equivalent conditions continued to ~8 g/L at 72h. The nominal source-calibrated forward model for KEEP predicts zero oxygen-deficit hours, minimum DO 5.76 mg/L (sensitivity range 3.14-6.91, all feasible), and terminal product mass ~576 kg. Since no oxygen constraint is being approached, feed reduction or aeration changes would sacrifice product mass without a compensating safety or feasibility gain. KEEP is the bounded, lowest-risk intervention.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; the hidden receiving realization may differ (model estimates transfer multiplier ~0.81). However, the large DO2 margin (9.2 vs 2.0 mg/L) makes an oxygen violation under KEEP unlikely; the sensitivity ensemble shows all members remain above the limit (min 3.14 mg/L). Product yield could vary somewhat, but interventions cannot improve feasibility and only risk mass loss. Assay availability lag (4h turnaround) means any measurement would be stale relative to the healthy online signal, so no extra assay was requested.
